# What we found after auditing 10,134 mem0 entries: 97.8% were junk

items.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Embedchain currently captures the publish date of YouTube videos but omits the precise publication time. 
The metadata stored for each video includes the date in the format YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00, which defaults to a time of 00:00:00, indicating that the time component is not being processed or stored.The issue with just the date is because of time zones.

Example of the issue: 
For a video published at 3 PM on April 15, 2024, Embedchain stores the publish date as 2024-04-15 00:00:00
Whereas it should be in ISO 8601 format ( example: 2024-04-15T14:30:00Z )
This forma
items.title: Unable to capture precise publication time for YouTube video metadata

items.body:
# Memory Lifetime Management via Forgetting Curve Model

## The Problem

Mem0 currently has no built-in mechanism for memory expiration or decay. Over time, local deployments accumulate stale entries that:
- Degrade retrieval quality (top-k results pollute context with outdated facts)
- Inflate token usage (obsolete memories consume context window)
- Create contradictions (stale preferences conflict with current ones)

## Solution: Forgetting Curve Model

We implemented a production-tested solution modeled after the Ebbinghaus forgetting curve — frequently accessed memories persist while unuse
items.title: Proposal: Memory access frequency tracking and lifetime-based cleanup
